name: PCA whitening
description: Decorrelate features via PCA followed by variance normalization. Preserves variance structure aligned with principal axes.

name: Averaged discriminative perceptron
description: Linear classifier with learned weights via mistake-driven update + averaging. Validated substrate-only on MAWPS 0.806, MultiArith 0.753 (2-op), CODE algorithm-pattern 0.750.

name: Bayesian inference
description: Posterior = likelihood * prior / evidence. General framework for substrate-stored posterior updates.

name: Dijkstra's algorithm
description: Single-source shortest-path algorithm for non-negative-weight graphs.

name: HMM transition probability
description: Probabilistic generative model component: probability of next state given current state P(state_{t+1} | state_t). Captures sequential structure in generative HMM framework. Used in Viterbi (max) and forward-backward (sum).

name: Answer-consistency weak labels
description: Weak-supervision method: for each training example, find latent assignment that makes the schema constraint yield the gold answer. Used in substrate MATH solver to train without role annotations.

name: Beam search
description: K-best approximate search keeping top-K candidates at each step. Trades optimality for tractability.

name: ZCA whitening
description: Zero-phase whitening; preserves orientation of original axes. Rotation-equivalent to PCA whitening.

name: Forward algorithm
description: DP for marginal observation likelihood under HMM. Sum over all state sequences.

name: Collins structured perceptron
description: Discriminative max-margin classifier with structured-output decoding (assignment-constraint enforcement). Learns weights via mistake-driven structured-perceptron update over joint feature representation. NOT probabilistic; max-margin formulation in structured output space.

name: Dynamic programming
description: Optimal substructure + overlapping subproblems via memoization. Foundation for Viterbi, MST, edit-distance, etc.

name: Hungarian algorithm
description: Polynomial-time optimal bipartite-matching algorithm minimizing total cost. Globally optimal over assignment polytope.

name: Perceptron weight update
description: Mistake-driven weight update: w += y*x on mistake. Foundation of perceptron and structured-perceptron learning.

name: HMM emission probability
description: Probabilistic generative model component: probability of observation given hidden state P(observation | state). Computed via count statistics (substrate-classical) or substrate Tier-2 schema. Used in Viterbi (max) and forward-backward (sum).

name: A* search
description: Heuristic-guided shortest-path search. Optimal with admissible heuristic.

name: Structured perceptron (Collins)
description: Collins 2002 discriminative max-margin classifier with structured-output decoding (assignment-constraint enforcement). Learns weights via mistake-driven structured-perceptron update over joint feature representation. NOT probabilistic; max-margin formulation in structured output space.

name: Viterbi decoder
description: O(N K^2) dynamic programming algorithm for max-product MAP decoding in HMM / chain CRF. Substrate-classical sequence decoder used in PP-364 POS Tier-A + PP-369 slot-filling Tier-B.

name: Viterbi decoding
description: Dynamic-programming algorithm for max-probability state sequence given observations. Globally optimal over linear chains.

name: Backward algorithm
description: DP for backward HMM probabilities. Used in EM and posterior decoding.

name: Expectation-maximization
description: Iterative algorithm for parameter estimation with latent variables. E-step computes posteriors; M-step maximizes parameters.

name: Forward algorithm
description: O(N K^2) dynamic programming for marginal posterior alpha_t(k) = P(o_1..o_t, x_t=k). Substrate companion to Viterbi for sum-product semiring.

name: MP bulk KL divergence
description: KL divergence of eigenvalue empirical density from Marchenko-Pastur bulk. Substrate Layer 2 measure of codebook deviation from random; substrate algebra-HRR codebook 12x semantic-bge per Findings 11 v2.1.

name: Backward algorithm
description: O(N K^2) dynamic programming for backward probability beta_t(k) = P(o_{t+1}..o_N | x_t=k). Substrate companion to forward for full posteriors + EM training.

name: Hungarian algorithm
description: Kuhn-Munkres O(N^3) algorithm for optimal bipartite matching with cost matrix. Substrate role-assigner primitive for discriminative-weighted matching.

name: Pointwise (Hadamard) product
description: Pointwise (Hadamard) product of two vectors: (a * b)_i = a_i * b_i. Elementwise multiplication; the operation that makes DFT-domain convolution-to-multiplication identity work.

name: DFT linearity lemma
description: DFT(a + b) = DFT(a) + DFT(b) AND DFT(c * a) = c * DFT(a) for scalar c. Linearity of the discrete Fourier transform; standard introductory property. Typed lemma; foundation for convolution_theorem_synthesis chain.

metadata.lemma: DFT(a + b) = DFT(a) + DFT(b); DFT(c*a) = c*DFT(a)

name: DFT convolution-to-pointwise lemma
description: DFT(conv(a, b)) = DFT(a) * DFT(b). The KEY lemma in the convolution theorem: convolution in the time domain becomes pointwise multiplication in the frequency domain. Foundation for fast convolution via DFT/FFT.

name: IDFT inverse property lemma
description: IDFT(DFT(v)) = v AND DFT(IDFT(v)) = v for any complex vector v. Inverse property of the discrete Fourier transform; the IDFT is the exact inverse (not just left-inverse). Required to invert the convolution-theorem identity.

name: Convolution theorem (synthesis)
description:
conv(a, b) = IDFT(DFT(a) * DFT(b)). The classical convolution theorem in the Z/N circular convention. Synthesized from DFT_convolution_to_pointwise_lemma (time-domain convolution equals frequency-domain pointwise product) and IDFT_inverse_property_lemma (apply IDFT to invert). DERIVATION:
  Premise 1 (DFT_convolution_to_pointwise): DFT(conv(a, b)) = DFT(a) * DFT(b)
  Premise 2 (IDFT_inverse_property): IDFT(DFT(v)) = v for any v
  Apply IDFT to both sides of premise 1: IDFT(DFT(conv(a, b))) = IDFT(DFT(a) * DFT(b))
  Substitute premise 2 on LHS (v := conv(a, b)): conv(a, b) = IDFT(DFT(a) * DFT(b))
  QED

derivation_steps: Apply IDFT to both sides: IDFT(DFT(conv(a, b))) = IDFT(DFT(a) * DFT(b))
Substitute on LHS: conv(a, b) = IDFT(DFT(a) * DFT(b))

name: Gradient-based optimizer (shared abstraction)
description: Shared abstraction over iterative optimizers that use the gradient of an objective function to update parameters. Iteration scheme: theta_{t+1} = theta_t - eta * F(g_t, ...) where g_t = nabla L(theta_t) and F is a method-specific update rule (identity for SGD; first/second moment estimates for Adam; etc.). Captures the common structure across gradient_descent + stochastic_gradient_descent + adam_optimizer (and other first-order methods). Per CELL-DISTILL-VERIFY-2 SHARED_ABSTRACTION verdict.

name: Product rule of probability (joint via conditional)
description: P(A ∩ B) = P(A|B) * P(B) = P(B|A) * P(A). Joint probability of two events factors via either conditioning direction. Foundational lemma; substrate-internal Bayes' rule derivation depends on this. Specialization of chain_rule_probability to two events.

metadata.lemma: P(A and B) = P(A|B) * P(B) = P(B|A) * P(A)

name: Bayes' rule (typed synthesis)
description:
P(A|B) = P(B|A) * P(A) / P(B) for P(B) > 0. Bayes' rule derived from product rule + conditional probability definition. DERIVATION:
  Premise 1 (product rule of probability): P(A ∩ B) = P(B|A) * P(A)
  Premise 2 (conditional probability definition): P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B)
  Substitute P1 into P2: P(A|B) = (P(B|A) * P(A)) / P(B)
  QED
Cross-domain bridge: measure-theoretic probability_space ↔ Bayesian inference (posterior = likelihood × prior / evidence).

derivation_steps: product_rule_probability: P(A and B) = P(B|A) * P(A)
conditional_probability_definition: P(A|B) = P(A and B) / P(B)

name: Characteristic function of iid sum (convolution-theorem in probability)
description: For independent random variables X_1, ..., X_n: phi_{X_1 + ... + X_n}(t) = phi_{X_1}(t) * ... * phi_{X_n}(t). The characteristic function of a sum of independent RVs equals the product of their characteristic functions. THIS IS THE CONVOLUTION THEOREM IN PROBABILITY: sum of iid corresponds to convolution of densities, which Fourier-transforms to pointwise product of characteristic functions. Cross-domain bridge to signal processing.

metadata.lemma: phi_{sum X_i}(t) = prod phi_{X_i}(t)  for independent X_i

name: Characteristic function Taylor expansion at zero
description: For random variable X with finite mean mu = E[X] and finite variance sigma^2 = Var(X), the characteristic function phi_X(t) admits the Taylor expansion at t=0: phi_X(t) = 1 + i*mu*t - (mu^2 + sigma^2)/2 * t^2 + o(t^2). Coefficients of the Taylor series correspond to moments of X (moment generating function correspondence). Required for CLT proof via characteristic function method.

name: Central Limit Theorem (typed synthesis via characteristic function)
description:
For iid X_1, ..., X_n with E[X_i] = mu and Var(X_i) = sigma^2 (finite), Z_n := (sum_i X_i - n*mu) / (sigma * sqrt(n)) converges in distribution to N(0, 1) as n -> infinity. DERIVATION (characteristic function method):
  Premise 1 (char-function of iid sum factorizes): phi_{sum X_i}(t) = (phi_X(t))^n
  Premise 2 (char-function Taylor expansion): phi_X(t/sqrt(n)) ~ 1 - t^2/(2n) for normalized RVs
  Premise 3 (exponential limit): (1 + x/n)^n -> exp(x) as n -> infinity
  Combine: phi_{Z_n}(t) -> exp(-t^2/2), which IS the characteristic function of N(0, 1)
  By the Levy continuity theorem, convergence of char-functions implies convergence in distribution
  QED
CROSS-DOMAIN: probability theory (iid sums) <-> Fourier analysis (characteristic function as Fourier transform of probability measure).

metadata.theorem: Z_n converges in distribution to N(0,1) for iid X_i with finite variance
derivation_steps: Combine: phi_{Z_n}(t) -> exp(-t^2/2) = char-function of N(0,1)
Levy continuity theorem: convergence of char-functions -> convergence in distribution

name: Self-adjoint operator property
description: Operator T on inner-product space H is self-adjoint iff <Tx, y> = <x, Ty> for all x, y in H. Equivalent to T* = T where T* is the adjoint. Self-adjoint operators are the bridge object between finite-dim linear algebra (symmetric matrices) and functional analysis (Hermitian operators on Hilbert space). Foundation for spectral theorem.

metadata.lemma: T self-adjoint iff <Tx, y> = <x, Ty> for all x, y in H

name: Self-adjoint operator has real eigenvalues
description: If T is self-adjoint and Tv = λv with v ≠ 0, then λ ∈ ℝ (i.e., λ = λ̄). Proof: λ<v,v> = <Tv, v> = <v, Tv> = <v, λv> = λ̄<v,v>. Since <v,v> > 0, divide to get λ = λ̄, so λ is real. This lemma is the FIRST PIECE of the spectral theorem proof.

metadata.lemma: T self-adjoint, Tv = λv, v ≠ 0 ⟹ λ ∈ ℝ

name: Spectral theorem (typed synthesis for self-adjoint operators)
description:
For a self-adjoint operator T on a finite-dim inner-product space H, there exists an orthonormal basis of H consisting of eigenvectors of T, and all eigenvalues of T are real. DERIVATION:
  Premise 1 (self_adjoint_operator): <Tx, y> = <x, Ty> for all x, y
  Premise 2 (real eigenvalues): λ ∈ ℝ for any eigenvalue (via P1)
  Premise 3 (eigenvectors with distinct λ orthogonal):
    If Tv_1 = λ_1 v_1, Tv_2 = λ_2 v_2, λ_1 ≠ λ_2:
    λ_1 <v_1, v_2> = <Tv_1, v_2> = <v_1, Tv_2> = λ_2 <v_1, v_2>
    So (λ_1 - λ_2)<v_1, v_2> = 0, and since λ_1 ≠ λ_2, <v_1, v_2> = 0.
  Synthesis: induct on dim(H). Take any eigenvector v_1 (exists in ℂ); consider H' = v_1^⊥; T restricts to a self-adjoint operator on H'; apply induction.
  Output: orthonormal eigenbasis {v_1, ..., v_n} with real eigenvalues {λ_1, ..., λ_n}
  QED
Cross-domain bridge: finite-dim linear algebra (symmetric matrices) ↔ functional analysis (self-adjoint operators on Hilbert space).

metadata.theorem: Self-adjoint T on finite-dim H admits orthonormal eigenbasis with real eigenvalues
derivation_steps: Induction on dim: orthonormal eigenbasis exists

name: Inner product positive semidefiniteness
description: For any vector w in an inner-product space H, <w, w> >= 0, with equality iff w = 0. This is the positive-semidefinite axiom of inner products. Used in the standard Cauchy-Schwarz derivation via the quadratic discriminant trick.

name: Nonnegative quadratic has nonpositive discriminant
description: If q(t) = a t^2 + b t + c with a >= 0 and q(t) >= 0 for all real t, then the discriminant b^2 - 4 a c <= 0. Proof: if the discriminant were positive, q would have two distinct real roots and would be negative between them, contradicting q(t) >= 0.

metadata.lemma: a>=0, q(t) = a t^2 + b t + c >= 0 for all t  =>  b^2 - 4 a c <= 0

name: Cauchy-Schwarz inequality (typed synthesis)
description:
For u, v in an inner-product space H: |<u, v>|^2 <= <u, u> * <v, v>. DERIVATION (quadratic discriminant trick):
  P1 (inner_product_positive_semidefinite): <u - t v, u - t v> >= 0 for all t in R
  P2 (expand by bilinearity): <u - tv, u - tv> = <u,u> - 2 t <u,v> + t^2 <v,v>
  P3 (quadratic_nonnegative_discriminant): quadratic q(t) = <v,v> t^2 - 2 <u,v> t + <u,u> is >= 0 for all t, so discriminant <= 0
  Compute discriminant: (-2<u,v>)^2 - 4 <v,v> <u,u> = 4 <u,v>^2 - 4 <u,u><v,v> <= 0
  Therefore: <u,v>^2 <= <u,u> <v,v>
  Equivalently: |<u,v>| <= ||u|| ||v|| (taking square root)
  QED
Cross-domain implications: |cos(angle(u,v))| <= 1 (geometry), cov(X,Y)^2 <= var(X) var(Y) (probability), |int f g| <= ||f||_2 ||g||_2 (analysis).

name: Inner product bilinearity
description: Inner product <,> is linear in each argument (over the relevant field). Specifically: <a u + b w, v> = a <u, v> + b <w, v> and similarly for the second argument (with possible conjugation for complex case). Foundation for expansion arguments like Pythagoras' theorem in inner-product spaces.

metadata.lemma: <au + bw, v> = a<u,v> + b<w,v>; symmetric on 2nd arg

name: Pythagoras theorem (inner-product space form)
description:
For u, v in an inner-product space H with <u, v> = 0 (orthogonal), ||u + v||^2 = ||u||^2 + ||v||^2. DERIVATION (1-step from bilinearity):
  ||u + v||^2 = <u+v, u+v>                          (def of norm)
              = <u,u> + <u,v> + <v,u> + <v,v>      (bilinearity)
              = <u,u> + 0 + 0 + <v,v>               (orthogonality)
              = ||u||^2 + ||v||^2                    (def of norm)
  QED
Cross-domain reach: classical Euclidean Pythagorean theorem (geometry) <-> inner-product spaces (functional analysis) <-> probability theory (variance additivity for uncorrelated random variables: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) when Cov(X,Y) = 0).

name: Vector space over a field
description: A set V together with a field F and operations (+: V x V -> V, scalar mul: F x V -> V) satisfying the 8 vector-space axioms. Type underlying linear_combination, basis, dimension, linear_operator.

name: Inner product space
description: Vector space V over R or C with a positive-definite Hermitian form <.,.>: V x V -> F. Type underlying norm-from-inner-product, orthogonality, projection, Cauchy-Schwarz, Pythagoras-in-IP.

name: Measurable space
description: Pair (X, Sigma) with sigma-algebra Sigma of subsets closed under complement and countable union. Type underlying measure, integration, probability_space, random_variable, conditional_expectation.

name: Linear operator (between vector spaces)
description: Map T: V -> W between vector spaces over the same field such that T(a*x + b*y) = a*T(x) + b*T(y). Type underlying matrices, bounded operators, self_adjoint, unitary, eigenvalue_problems.

name: Bilinear form
description: Map B: V x V -> F linear in each argument (with possible conjugation in 2nd arg over C). Type underlying inner_product, quadratic_form, Gram matrix, symmetric and Hermitian forms.

name: Continuous map (between topological spaces)
description: Function f: X -> Y between topological_spaces such that preimage of every open set is open. Type underlying homeomorphism, differentiable maps, integrable functions, paths.

name: Self-adjoint operator (type)
description: Bounded operator T on Hilbert space with <Tx, y> = <x, Ty> for all x, y. Type underlying spectral_theorem, real_eigenvalues, observable in quantum mechanics, covariance_operator. DISTINCT from T3/self_adjoint_operator_lemma which asserts the property.

name: Random variable (type)
description: Measurable function X: Omega -> R from probability_space (Omega, F, P) to R with Borel sigma-algebra. Type underlying expectation, variance, characteristic_function, distribution, conditional_expectation, CLT.

name: Measure-preserving map
description: Map T: (X, F, mu) -> (X, F, mu) on measure_space with mu(T^{-1}(A)) = mu(A) for all A in F. Type underlying ergodic_theorem, dynamical_systems, stationary_processes, Poincare_recurrence.

name: Group action (type)
description: Map G x X -> X for group G and set X satisfying identity and compatibility axioms. Type underlying symmetry, orbit, stabilizer, representation_theory, equivariant_maps.
